About me

Intimate realism with a philosophical undertow.

I am a Romanian filmmaker currently based in Sheffield, UK.

I studied Physics and Philosophy at the University of Sheffield, though over time cinema became the medium through which I felt most able to explore memory, estrangement, intimacy, and the quiet emotional tensions of everyday life.

I’m drawn to grounded, observational storytelling shaped by atmosphere, restraint, and a sense of poetry within ordinary spaces. My work has been influenced by filmmakers such as Wong Kar Wai, Wim Wenders, Luca Guadagnino, and Martin Scorsese.

I began working in film on Radu Jude’s I Do Not Care If We Go Down in History as Barbarians (2018) before continuing across a range of productions, from independent grassroots filmmaking to larger professional sets. In 2022, I helped revive and expand the Sheffield Filmmaking Society following the pandemic, contributing to a growing local filmmaking community.

My latest short film, Embers in the Kitchen, is currently being submitted to international film festivals, while several new projects are in development.
